pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Acute Thallium Poisoning THE SMOKING GUN: The triad of severe painful axonal neuropathy, autonomic instability, and delayed rapid-onset diffuse alopecia (occurring 10-14 days post-exposure). PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Thallium acts as a cellular toxin due to its ionic radius being nearly identical to potassium, allowing it to compete with potassium at the Na+/K+-ATPase membrane pump. Once inside cells, it cross-links sulfhydryl groups on vital enzymes, uncouples oxidative phosphorylation, and disrupts riboflavin kinase. High-energy and high-turnover tissues are preferentially devastated, leading to distal axonal nerve degeneration, mucosal lining breakdown, and loss of hair follicle integrity.
